decision_triggers: If line_loss_events stays at 1 on the S-bend or slalom with 0.6 kg, the loss is not geometric. Check the controller line_loss handling and the start position before changing geometry again.
If line_loss_events is 0 but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the next geometry step is wheel_track 0.12 m for more turn authority, since body_width cannot move the limit.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
integration_questions: With mass at 0.6 kg, does the robot overshoot less on the S-bend and slalom at the same kp and kd, or does the lighter body make steering oscillation worse?
Does the line-loss event on the S-bend and slalom disappear at +/-0.05 m? If it persists, at what position on the course does it start?
Do the outer sensors at +/-0.05 m read zero on most of the course, and does the signal still stay monotonic across the full span?

intent: Keep the +/-0.05 m, 16 mm sensor array at y = 0.04 m that removed oval line loss in iteration 3, and reduce mass from 0.7 kg to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia and bend overshoot. Expected: line_loss_events at 0 on the oval, S-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 m, and higher progress on the S-bend and slalom than iteration 3.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that span removes oval line loss but not S-bend or slalom loss, so the span is necessary but not sufficient. The next test separates mass-driven overshoot from a non-geometric loss. Record whether max_error falls with mass and whether the S-bend and slalom losses clear.
rationale: Iteration 3 widened the outer sensors to x = +/-0.05 m, and line_loss_events fell to 0 on the oval, though the score only rose to 55.27. The S-bend and slalom still logged one loss each, and every run ended off_track with max_error about 0.064 m, which is above the fixed 0.06 m limit. Progress stayed at 0.11 to 0.17, so runs are being lost early on the first sharp bends rather than late in the course. Body_width cannot move the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) stays at 0.06 m for bw of 0.12 m), so the remaining lever is dynamic: the robot overshoots the bends. Iteration 1 showed that a higher kp raises oscillation, so the controller alone cannot fix this. Mass sets yaw inertia and momentum, and the earlier feedback named 0.6 kg as the next step once line loss is geometrically closed. I therefore keep the iteration 3 span (+/-0.05 m) and 16 mm footprints, which removed the oval loss, and reduce mass from 0.7 kg to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia and bend overshoot. Body width, wheel radius, wheel track and body length stay fixed to isolate the mass effect. Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 m on the S-bend and slalom, line_loss_events goes to 0 on all three tracks, and progress rises above the iteration 3 level. If line loss stays at 1 on the S-bend or slalom at 0.6 kg, the loss is not geometric, and the controller line_loss handling or start position should be checked before any further geometry change.
